objective: The catalogue field that says at which stock level an item should be reordered is called `reorder_level` on `Item`, which reads like a current level rather than a threshold. Rename the field to `reorder_point` throughout the code (the record, the code that reads and writes it, the stock check and the sample data script). Only the name in the code changes: the CSV column is still called `reorder_level`, and the messages, help texts and output that mention it keep their wording, because files and scripts outside this repository depend on them. Code that only reads `item.reorder_level` must keep working through a read-only alias. The existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: The fields of `Item` are `sku`, `name`, `price_cents`, `tags`, `reorder_point`, in this order; `reorder_point` defaults to 0, can be passed positionally or by keyword, and appears in `repr` and `dataclasses.asdict`; equality and hashing of items are unchanged
Validation messages are unchanged: a negative reorder point gives `ParseError` `<sku>: negative reorder level`, a negative price `<sku>: negative price`
`Item.reorder_level` is still readable and returns the reorder point; it is a read-only property, not a dataclass field
Outside the alias definition in `stockroom/models.py`, no code in the `stockroom` package or in `scripts/` uses the name `reorder_level` as an attribute, keyword argument, parameter or variable

The file format is unchanged: `ITEM_HEADER` still ends with the column `reorder_level`, `read_items` of a file with that header fills `reorder_point`, `write_items` writes the same text as before (so the round trip of a catalogue file is identical), a bad number gives `line N: reorder_level is not a whole number: ...`, and a header with the column `reorder_point` is refused with `item header must be sku,name,price,tags,reorder_level`
`Inventory.low_stock(items)` returns the items whose available stock is below their reorder point, in the given order
`stockroom stock` prints the same `LOW ...` lines and the same `warning: N item(s) below reorder level` line as before, and the help texts that mention the reorder level are unchanged
`scripts/make_sample_data.py` writes byte-identical files for the same seed and order count
